gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 limits its car-port charging input to 8 A at 12–16 V, which is about 96–128 W and takes around 12 hours to fill. Jackery says this in its own words. The bigger possible failure, the low-load auto-off timers that can switch off a cycling compressor fridge, I could not source from a maker page I opened.
standout_why: I opened the two pages ChatGPT cited and two top results. Cited yourpowersetup.com lists only solar voltage windows (C1000 Gen 2 11–60 V, DELTA 3 Plus 11–60 V per input, Jackery 1000 v2 16–60 V). It has no charge temperature, car-input watts, idle draw or auto-off rules. Cited greenmachineadventures.com says only 'follow its charging and operating-temperature limits' and names an 800 W alternator charger for the DELTA 3 Plus, with no input limits or auto-off rules. Uncited result #6, outagereadyhq.com, already gives the 32°F charging floor for the Anker and the Jackery, a 12-hour car-adapter charge time for the Jackery (without watts or amps), 800 W car input for the DELTA 3 Plus, and the car-socket outputs. solarwaypoint.com has none of this. So only the Jackery 8 A / 12–16 V input limit is new, and the 0 °C charging floor is already partly covered.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick. For car campers who plan to recharge from the vehicle's 12 V socket, the Jackery 1000 v2 tops up at only about 100 W, roughly 12 hours for a full charge, and only above freezing (0 °C / 32°F). For campers who recharge while driving, that favours the DELTA 3 Plus, which takes up to 800 W through EcoFlow's separate alternator charger according to outagereadyhq. All three stop charging below freezing, so cold-weather campers have to rely on stored energy whatever they pick.

findings.label: Car-port charging input
findings.value: 12–16 V, current limit 8 A; around 12 h to full via the car charger port (around 3 h with the separate car fast charger)
findings.source_title: Explorer 1000 V2 Basic Information (Jackery Help Center)
findings.note: 12 V × 8 A = 96 W; 16 V × 8 A = 128 W. 1,070 Wh ÷ ~96 W ≈ 11 h, which matches Jackery's 'around 12H'.

findings.source_title: Explorer 1000 V2 Basic Information (Jackery Help Center)
findings.note: Below 0 °C it won't take a charge from solar, the car or the wall.

findings.source_title: Explorer 1000 V2 Basic Information (Jackery Help Center)
findings.note: Enough for a typical 12 V compressor fridge, which saves the inverter loss of running it from AC.
